title: Split-brain drain reconciliation caused sticky cross-region routing and variant starvation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
summary: During a multi-region maintenance window a split-brain condition in the routing control plane allowed conflicting drain signals to be applied in different orders. The control plane reconciler's non-monotonic tombstone handling produced a flip-flop of decommission markers; requests became sticky to a partially drained region and routing fell back to a narrow set of model variants that were effectively unreachable, producing increased latency, a spike in fallback errors, and downstream customer impact for ~70 minutes.
timeline: 2025-02-14 01:10 UTC: Scheduled regional maintenance began; control-plane upgrade triggers rolling restart of regional controllers.
2025-02-14 01:24 UTC: Inconsistent ordering of decommission operations observed between us-east and eu-west controllers (heartbeat delay ~12s).
2025-02-14 01:28 UTC: Route reconciliation applied a tombstone with older timestamp which caused route entries to revert; traffic remained pinned (sticky) to us-east for ~15 minutes.
2025-02-14 01:40 UTC: Fallback surge detected as primary variants in us-east hit eviction thresholds; fallback attempts targeted variants mapped to eu-west which had stale variant mappings.
2025-02-14 01:45 UTC: Alerts triggered (high p99 latency, error-rate on fallback paths); on-call routed to runtime and routing teams.
2025-02-14 02:05 UTC: Mitigation: rolled back routing control-plane canary and enabled immediate tombstone expiry override; prefetched KV cache for critical variants in healthy regions.
2025-02-14 02:20 UTC: Traffic rebalanced successfully; p95/p99 latencies returned to normal by 02:40 UTC.
impact: Approximately 70 minutes of degraded routing for a subset of customers (mostly mid-to-large customers with region affinity). Observed symptoms: increased token latency (p99 up 2.5x), elevated 5xx rates on fallback calls, and a small number of model invocation failures that triggered customer-visible retries. Estimated affected requests: ~1.4M.
root_cause: Control-plane reconciliation used wall-clock timestamps from regional controllers without a monotonic epoch. Concurrent decommission signals applied in different orders produced tombstone flip-flops. The routing evaluation logic treats the latest-seen tombstone timestamp as authoritative even when it represents an out-of-order write, which allowed stale tombstones to override newer decommissions. The combination of sticky session affinity (session cookies + client IP affinity) and stale variant mapping in the fallback table led to variant starvation: fallback requests were routed to variants whose serving endpoints had already been drained or whose KV caches were cold, amplifying latency and failure rates.
detection: On-call alerts for increased fallback error rate and p99 token latency. Runtime dashboards showed rising tombstone_flip_rate and per-region sticky_ratio. A correlation between tombstone write churn and spike in fallback latency was discovered by tracing the control-plane event log and comparing controller epochs.
mitigation_taken: Rollback: Reverted the control-plane change introduced in runtime-1.20 canary in the eu-west controller (02:05 UTC).
Immediate config: Enabled tombstone expiry override for affected regions to force decommissions to finish and prevent flip-flops (02:10 UTC).
Cache warm-up: Triggered warmup jobs to pre-populate KV caches for critical fallbacks in healthy regions (02:12 UTC).
Traffic shift: Applied conservative routing override to prefer healthy regions with confirmed controller epochs until reconciliation completed (02:20 UTC).
permanent_fixes: Introduce monotonic decommission epoch numbers (per-region, globally comparable) — routing writes must include epoch and be accepted only if epoch >= current.
Change routing reconciler to use CAS-style updates with vector clocks for control-plane objects to avoid non-linear timestamp wins.
Remove reliance on wall-clock timestamps for tombstone ordering; add tombstone_flip_rate metric and an alert when flip rate exceeds threshold.
Make session affinity relaxed during active decommission windows (feature-flagged): allow ephemeral affinity drain with TTL to prevent long-lived stickiness.
Add preemptive fallback health-checks and a 'variant reachability' probe that marks variants unreachable when KV cold-starts exceed threshold.
Extend runbook with explicit steps for tombstone override, controller epoch inspection, and safe reconciliation procedure.
verification: Post-deploy monitoring (runtime-1.20 patch) showed tombstone_flip_rate dropped to zero, per-region sticky_ratio returned to baseline within 15 minutes of deploy. End-to-end canary traffic passed 2 hours of sustained load test using the new CAS reconciler. New unit + integration tests added to control-plane test harness; synthetic variants with cold caches were included in chaos tests.

postmortem_notes: This incident exposed a subtle consistency assumption in the routing control plane: that timestamps across regions would be comparable during rolling upgrades. That assumption is unsafe during network/upgrade windows. The fixes favor stronger coordination and atomicity over a best-effort timestamp model. We chose a short rollback and cache-warmup mitigation to reduce customer impact while prioritizing a correct long-term fix that changes reconciliation semantics. CM/Legal notified about customer impact; no PII exposure was detected.
